chunks: Praise is due to Allah, whose worth cannot be described by speakers, whose bounties cannot be counted by calculators, and whose claim cannot be satisfied by those who strive to do so,
whom the height of intellectual courage cannot appreciate, and the divings of understanding cannot reach;
He for whose description no limit has been laid down, no eulogy exists, no time is ordained and no duration is fixed.
He brought forth creation through His Omnipotence, dispersed winds through His Compassion, and made firm the shaking earth with rocks.
ai.seo_question: What are the divine attributes of Allah described in Nahj al-Balagha's description of creation?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the concept of *Tawhid al-Sifat* (Oneness of Attributes), emphasizing Allah's transcendence (*Tanzih*) beyond human comprehension and linguistic limitation. The text highlights the divine act of creation (*Fitrah*) as a manifestation of mercy and power, a theme central to Shia theological discourse on the relationship between the Creator and the cosmos. This reflection serves as a profound meditation on the limits of human intellect (*Aql*) when confronting the infinite nature of the Divine.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Praise is due to Allāh whose worth cannot be described by speakers, whose bounties cannot be counted by calculators and whose claim (to obedience) cannot be satisfied by those who attempt to do so,
whom the height of intellectual courage cannot appreciate, and the divings of understanding cannot reach;
He for whose description no limit has been laid down, no eulogy exists, no time is ordained and no duration is fixed.
He brought forth creation through His Omnipotence, dispersed winds through His Compassion, and made firm the shaking earth with rocks.
